prompt: It is often argued that every town and city should provide large public outdoor areas such as parks and squares. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that every town and city should provide large public outdoor areas, such as parks and squares, for its residents. I strongly agree with this view because such spaces can promote physical and psychological well-being while also creating opportunities for meaningful social interaction.

One significant advantage of accessible outdoor facilities is their contribution to public health. When residents have convenient access to parks and open areas, they are more likely to walk, exercise and spend time outside. For example, a well-designed urban park may include walking paths, playgrounds and open spaces for recreational activities. People can consequently maintain a more active lifestyle while taking a break from the pressures of urban living. This can improve physical fitness and contribute to better psychological well-being.

Green surroundings can also provide relief from the stressful atmosphere of crowded cities. Although urban life is often associated with noise and constant activity, a quiet park can offer residents a place to relax. Someone who spends time walking among trees after a demanding day, for instance, may feel calmer and mentally refreshed. In this respect, outdoor facilities serve purposes that extend beyond simple recreation.

Beyond their health benefits, public outdoor areas can foster stronger community ties. Because parks and squares are shared spaces, people from different age groups and social backgrounds have opportunities to meet and communicate. A clear illustration of this is a city square that hosts cultural festivals, weekend markets or community programmes. Such activities bring residents together, encourage informal interaction and gradually strengthen their sense of belonging. In this way, public spaces serve not merely as recreational facilities but also as platforms for community engagement.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that every town and city should provide substantial public outdoor areas. They encourage healthier lifestyles, offer relief from urban pressures and create opportunities for residents to interact. Such facilities are therefore an essential component of well-planned cities.
